boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Arizona
boards.description: Ten currently documented food destinations with late availability in Tucson, centered on campus and nearby corridors.

cards.title: Turkish Kebab House
cards.subtitle: 810 E University Blvd · open daily until 2 AM
cards.notes: Use the Main Gate Square address for a seated or takeout meal; check the official hours before heading over, especially on holidays.
cards.short_summary: A University Boulevard Turkish and Mediterranean restaurant with daily late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The restaurant’s official site lists its 810 E University Blvd address and business hours of 8:30 AM–2 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Turkish Kebab House
cards.access_notes: Official site lists daily business hours of 8:30 AM–2 AM.

cards.title: Arabic Express
cards.subtitle: 806 E University Blvd · takeout listed until 1 AM
cards.notes: Order pickup or delivery from the University Boulevard location when you need a food option after typical dinner hours; confirm timing in advance.
cards.short_summary: A Middle Eastern restaurant at the campus-side end of University Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: Arabic Express’s official ordering site identifies 806 E University Boulevard and lists takeout hours until 1 AM on listed days.
cards.source_title: Arabic Express
cards.access_notes: Official ordering page lists takeout through 1 AM on Monday–Friday and Sunday; Saturday is listed through midnight.

cards.title: Geronimo Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 806 E University Blvd · takeout listed until 1 AM
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online ordering page to check pickup hours and place an order; the location sits directly on the University Boulevard corridor.
cards.short_summary: A late-listed breakfast and American-food pickup option near the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Geronimo Restaurant’s official ordering page lists 806 E University Blvd and takeout operation until 1 AM on listed days.
cards.source_title: Geronimo Restaurant
cards.access_notes: Official ordering page lists takeout until 1 AM Monday–Friday and Sunday, and until midnight Saturday.

cards.title: Fuku Sushi
cards.subtitle: 940 E University Blvd · open until 2 AM Tue–Sat
cards.notes: Check the posted daily schedule before going; the restaurant lists midnight hours on Sunday and Monday and later hours Tuesday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A sushi restaurant on University Boulevard with late posted closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Fuku Sushi’s official site lists 940 E University Blvd and hours until 2 AM Tuesday–Saturday, with midnight closing Sunday and Monday.
cards.source_title: Fuku Sushi
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 11 AM–2 AM Tuesday–Saturday and 11 AM–midnight Sunday and Monday.

cards.entity_name: Shark's Grill at U of A South Rec
cards.title: Shark's Grill at U of A South Rec
cards.subtitle: U of A South Rec · 7–11 PM Mon–Fri
cards.notes: Find the truck at U of A South Rec on weekday evenings and use its official location page to verify service before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A campus food-truck stop with documented weekday evening service.
cards.evidence_claim: Shark’s Grill’s official site lists its U of A South Rec location as open 7–11 PM Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Shark's Grill AZ — About
cards.access_notes: Official site lists U of A South Rec service Monday–Friday, 7 PM–11 PM; closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.entity_name: Jack in the Box — 1055 N Park Ave
cards.title: Jack in the Box on Park Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1055 N Park Ave · lobby listed until 4 AM daily
cards.notes: Use the Park Avenue location if you need a walk-in option after late evening; verify the location page for any holiday or temporary changes.
cards.short_summary: A Park Avenue fast-food location with 4 AM lobby hours listed every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack in the Box’s official location page lists lobby hours at 1055 N Park Ave as open until 4 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Jack in the Box — 1055 N Park Ave
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists lobby hours from 4 AM to 4 AM daily, indicating continuous daily availability.

cards.title: Wendy's on North Campbell
cards.subtitle: 1005 N Campbell Ave · open until 1 AM Thu–Sat
cards.notes: Choose restaurant or drive-thru service at this campus-area address; check the official schedule because closing shifts between midnight and 1 AM.
cards.short_summary: A North Campbell fast-food restaurant with midnight-or-later posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru service until 1 AM Thursday–Saturday and until midnight on other days.
cards.source_title: Wendy's — 1005 N Campbell Ave
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until midnight Sunday–Wednesday and 1 AM Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Del Taco on East Broadway
cards.subtitle: 840 E Broadway Blvd · open until midnight most days
cards.notes: Use this Broadway location for a late pickup, delivery, or dine-in stop; the official page shows a slightly earlier Sunday close.
cards.short_summary: A downtown-adjacent taco location with midnight hours on six days each week.
cards.evidence_claim: Del Taco’s official location page lists the 840 E Broadway Blvd store open until midnight Monday–Saturday and until 11 PM Sunday.
cards.source_title: Del Taco — 840 E Broadway Blvd
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists store and delivery hours until midnight Monday–Saturday; Sunday until 11 PM.

cards.title: Taco Plus Mexican Grub
cards.subtitle: 4352 E Speedway Blvd · open 24 hours Tue–Sun
cards.notes: This is farther east on Speedway, so plan transportation; use the official page’s posted schedule and order link before going late.
cards.short_summary: A Speedway Boulevard Mexican fast-food stop with six days of 24-hour service listed.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Plus Mexican Grub’s official site lists 24-hour service Tuesday–Sunday and Monday service until midnight.
cards.source_title: Taco Plus Mexican Grub
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Tuesday–Sunday as open 24 hours and Monday as 7 AM–midnight.

cards.title: El Potosino Mexican Food
cards.subtitle: 1400 W Prince Rd · open 24 hours daily
cards.notes: Plan a ride to the Prince Road location and confirm availability before leaving; the restaurant’s own menu page identifies it as a 24-hour operation.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Mexican-food restaurant for an all-night Tucson option beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: El Potosino’s official menu page states that its 1400 W Prince Rd location is open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: El Potosino Mexican Restaurant — Tacos
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Monday–Sunday hours as 24 hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Arizona spaces for studying, making, relaxing, and connecting between classes.

cards.title: Main Library
cards.subtitle: 1510 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Start on the floor that matches your task: use group rooms for collaboration or head upward for listed quiet-study floors.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor library with group rooms, quiet rooms, technology, and research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library lists group study rooms, quiet study rooms, a quiet study floor, computers, CATalyst Studios, and Scholars' Corner.
cards.source_title: Main Library | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Library spaces are available during open hours; access varies by user status and space.

cards.title: Scholars' Corner
cards.subtitle: Main Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use this named Main Library work area when you want a shared indoor place to settle in between classes or research tasks.
cards.short_summary: A named walk-in work area inside the Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries identifies Scholars' Corner as a walk-in library space and lists it on the Main Library's second floor.
cards.source_title: Rooms and spaces | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Walk in during library open hours; the library notes that access may vary by individual status.

cards.title: CATalyst Studios
cards.subtitle: Main Library, second floor
cards.notes: Plan a project session here when your work calls for creating or collaborating rather than a conventional reading-room setup.
cards.short_summary: A named creative studio located on the Main Library's second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library floor listing places CATalyst Studios on its second floor, and the library describes its spaces as places to study, meet, and collaborate.
cards.source_title: Main Library | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current access guidance and open hours before visiting.

cards.title: Maker Studio
cards.subtitle: University of Arizona Libraries
cards.notes: Drop in during open hours to work in a library maker space, then confirm any equipment or project requirements with staff.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in University Libraries space for students, faculty, staff, and community users.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists Maker Studio among its walk-in spaces and says walk-in spaces need no reservation during open hours.
cards.source_title: Rooms and spaces | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for this walk-in space during library open hours.

cards.title: Tech Zone
cards.subtitle: University of Arizona Libraries
cards.notes: Use this walk-in library space when technology is part of the task, and check in with library staff for current support details.
cards.short_summary: A named walk-in technology-oriented space in the University Libraries system.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists Tech Zone as a walk-in space available to students, faculty, staff, and community users.
cards.source_title: Rooms and spaces | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for walk-in spaces during library open hours.

cards.title: Student Union Memorial Center
cards.subtitle: Central campus
cards.notes: Meet a friend, find a seat, join a campus activity, or use the building as a between-classes gathering point; follow access rules.
cards.short_summary: The campus student union combines dining, activities, and spaces to relax or connect.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Student Unions describes the Student Union Memorial Center as serving students and the campus community from the heart of campus, with spaces to unwind, activities, and dining.
cards.source_title: Student Unions Overview | Arizona Student Unions
cards.access_notes: Use is intended for students, faculty, staff, university guests, and authorized activity participants.

cards.title: Student Success District
cards.subtitle: Central campus, near Main Library
cards.notes: Grab a table or chair here for a study break, focused work, or a low-key meeting; outdoor seating includes wifi and charger access.
cards.short_summary: A student-support district with tables, chairs, wifi, and nearby charger boxes.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arizona Student Success says students can study, relax, and find community in free spaces including the Student Success District, and notes nearby seating with wifi and charger boxes.
cards.source_title: Student Resources | University of Arizona Student Success
cards.access_notes: The university identifies tables and chairs here as free spaces for students to study, relax, and find community.

cards.title: Main Mall
cards.subtitle: Central campus pedestrian mall
cards.notes: Take your work outside on the mall when the weather suits it, using campus wifi and choosing a seating area that fits your group.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed central campus mall with outdoor wifi access.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arizona Student Success identifies the mall as an outdoor campus location where wifi is accessible, and the official campus map labels the Main Mall.
cards.source_title: Student Resources | University of Arizona Student Success
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; consult campus guidance for scheduled activities or restricted areas.

cards.title: Turtle Pond
cards.subtitle: University of Arizona campus
cards.notes: Use the nearby outdoor setting for a quiet pause or informal study session, keeping clear of any posted rules and active campus events.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor campus spot identified by Student Success as having wifi access nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arizona Student Success specifically names turtle pond among outdoor campus places where wifi is accessible.
cards.source_title: Student Resources | University of Arizona Student Success
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; follow posted campus rules and respect wildlife and landscaping.

cards.title: Krutch Garden
cards.subtitle: Near Old Main on the official campus map
cards.notes: Build a short outdoor reset into your route through central campus, then continue to nearby study and student-service destinations.
cards.short_summary: A named garden shown on the University of Arizona's official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: The official University of Arizona property map labels Krutch Garden near Old Main and the Main Mall.
cards.source_title: University of Arizona Property Map
cards.access_notes: Use the live campus map for current routing and any access changes.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time together on campus and in nearby Tucson public spaces.

cards.entity_name: University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.title: Browse the University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 1031 N. Olive Road, campus Arts Oasis
cards.notes: Meet at the entrance, choose a gallery together, and take a slow lap before comparing the work that held everyone’s attention.
cards.short_summary: A free all-visitor art-museum visit on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UAMA lists admission as free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Hours, Admission, Directions | The University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; closed Sunday, Monday, and holidays. Parking may cost extra.

cards.title: See “Animality: 100 Years of Photographs”
cards.subtitle: Center for Creative Photography, 1030 N. Olive Road
cards.notes: Use the galleries as a conversation prompt: pick one animal image each, then regroup to share what you noticed in its framing or story.
cards.short_summary: A current free exhibition of photography from CCP’s collection.
cards.evidence_claim: CCP’s “Animality: 100 Years of Photographs” is free and open to the public through December 12, 2026.
cards.source_title: A century of looking at animals and ourselves
cards.access_notes: The exhibition runs August 8-December 12, 2026; gallery hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m.

cards.entity_name: African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.title: Visit the African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.subtitle: Student Union, Room 244
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided visit with friends, then pause on one story, image, or artifact that gives your group a question to carry forward.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum documenting Black life and history in Southern Arizona.
cards.evidence_claim: AAMSAZ states that general admission is free and identifies its campus location in Student Union Room 244.
cards.source_title: Sign up for Tours and Visits | African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.access_notes: Visitors are welcomed Wednesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; the museum asks visitors to contact it or submit a request before visiting.

cards.title: Attend a Poetry Center reading
cards.subtitle: 1508 E. Helen Street
cards.notes: Check the reading calendar, arrive a few minutes early, and stay afterward to trade a favorite line or image with the people you came with.
cards.short_summary: Live readings at the campus Poetry Center carry no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Poetry Center FAQ says its poetry readings are all free to attend.
cards.source_title: FAQ | Poetry Center
cards.access_notes: The Poetry Center library is open to the public; consult its calendar for individual reading dates and times.

cards.title: Explore Special Collections
cards.subtitle: 1510 E. University Boulevard, beside Main Library
cards.notes: Choose a collection theme before you go, then ask staff how to view a related item or exhibit without trying to rush the visit.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing archive of rare books, photographs, recordings, and manuscripts.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries says Special Collections is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: University of Arizona Libraries & Research Resources
cards.access_notes: Special Collections is open to everyone Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m.; check its detailed hours before visiting.

cards.title: Digitize a shared memory at Wildcats Memory Lab
cards.subtitle: Main Library, Room B302
cards.notes: Bring a photo, tape, or audio item you are allowed to copy, and make a small project of preserving it together in the lab.
cards.short_summary: A public DIY lab for digitizing personal media.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes Wildcats Memory Lab as open to the public for personal archiving and says it is free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Wildcats Memory Lab Grand Opening and Open House
cards.access_notes: Located in Main Library Room B302 on the third floor; confirm current lab availability before bringing media.

cards.title: Follow the Old Main tree walk
cards.subtitle: UA Campus Arboretum at Old Main
cards.notes: Start with the arboretum’s Old Main guide, take photos of labeled trees, and let each person choose one plant to look up afterward.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided botanical walk around the university’s historic first building.
cards.evidence_claim: The UA Campus Arboretum says campus is open seven days a week and absolutely free, and offers an Old Main tour.
cards.source_title: Old Main Tour | UA Campus Arboretum
cards.access_notes: The campus is open seven days a week. Free arboretum booklets may be borrowed from Herring Hall during weekday business hours.

cards.title: Take the Main Library tree walk
cards.subtitle: UA Campus Arboretum around Main Library
cards.notes: Use the arboretum’s Main Library walk as a low-key route, stopping at labeled trees and saving one unfamiliar species for a group photo.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided campus tree route centered on Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library arboretum walk states that campus is open seven days a week and absolutely free.
cards.source_title: A Walk Around the Main Library
cards.access_notes: The guide notes that self-guided arboretum booklets are available for loan from Herring Hall during weekday business hours.

cards.title: Go for a swim at Catalina Pool
cards.subtitle: City of Tucson year-round pool
cards.notes: Bring water and sun protection, agree on a meet-up time, and use the free pool visit for laps, floating, or a simple cool-down together.
cards.short_summary: A City of Tucson pool with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Tucson lists Catalina Pool as a year-round pool and says admission to all city pools and splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splash Pads | City of Tucson
cards.access_notes: Catalina Pool is listed as year-round. Check the City of Tucson schedule for operating hours and any closure notices.

cards.title: Meet up for a Fort Lowell Pool swim
cards.subtitle: City of Tucson extended-season pool
cards.notes: Make it a daytime plan: pack what you need, set a check-in point, and give everyone room to swim, relax, or cheer on a lap challenge.
cards.short_summary: An extended-season City of Tucson pool with no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Tucson lists Fort Lowell Pool as an extended-season pool and says admission to all city pools and splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splash Pads | City of Tucson
cards.access_notes: Fort Lowell Pool is listed as approximately May-October. Check the City of Tucson schedule for current hours and closures.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, source-backed University of Arizona library environments for quiet reading, group work, computer tasks, and project-based study.

cards.title: Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Main Library, room C318
cards.notes: Bring reading or offline work and silence every device before entering; the room’s rule is no sound, including whispers, keyboards, or headphones.
cards.short_summary: A first-come Main Library room designed for absolute silence.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library’s Silent Study Room is C318 on the third floor and is first come, first served during open hours; no sound is permitted.
cards.source_title: Silent study room | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: First come, first served when the library is open; room C318 is on Main Library’s third floor.

cards.title: Scholars’ Corner
cards.subtitle: Main Library, A220
cards.notes: Use the CatCard entrance on the second floor and choose a window seat for individual work or a small, low-key conversation with collaborators.
cards.short_summary: A 14-seat, naturally lit room with monitors and an adjacent patio.
cards.evidence_claim: Scholars’ Corner in Main Library room A220 has large windows, natural light, LCD monitors, seating for up to 14, and permits small-group work.
cards.source_title: Scholars' Corner | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: For UA graduate students, honors undergraduates, and faculty; first come, first served during open hours. CatCard access required.

cards.entity_name: Main Library Quiet Study Area, Floor 4
cards.title: Main Library Quiet Study Area — Floor 4
cards.subtitle: Main Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor for a quieter session, keep mobile devices silent, and save any extended conversation for the floor lobby.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Main Library floor with seating and whiteboards nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library floor 4 is a designated quiet-study floor; quiet-study areas include comfy seating and whiteboards and are first come, first served when open.
cards.source_title: Quiet study areas | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available first come, first served when the library is open; speak quietly and limit louder conversation to the floor lobby.

cards.entity_name: Main Library Quiet Study Area, Floor 5
cards.title: Main Library Quiet Study Area — Floor 5
cards.subtitle: Main Library, fifth floor
cards.notes: Settle in on the fifth floor for focused reading or writing, silence your phone, and take calls or louder collaboration back to the lobby.
cards.short_summary: A separate quiet floor above Main Library’s fourth-floor study area.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library floor 5 is a designated quiet-study floor, where the Libraries direct users to speak quietly, silence mobile devices, and use the lobby for louder conversation.
cards.source_title: Quiet study areas | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available first come, first served when the library is open.

cards.entity_name: Weaver Library Quiet Study Area, Floor 1
cards.title: Weaver Quiet Study Area — Floor 1
cards.subtitle: Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library, first floor
cards.notes: Choose the first-floor quiet area for independent work, keep devices silent, and use the floor lobby if your discussion needs more volume.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study floor inside the science and engineering library.
cards.evidence_claim: The first floor of Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library is a designated quiet-study floor with seating and whiteboards in several areas.
cards.source_title: Quiet study areas | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available first come, first served when the library is open; follow the quiet-area expectation for devices and conversations.

cards.entity_name: Weaver Library Quiet Study Area, Floor 4
cards.title: Weaver Quiet Study Area — Floor 4
cards.subtitle: Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Use this upper-floor quiet area for concentrated coursework; silence mobile devices and move calls or louder project talk to the floor lobby.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor quiet option near Weaver’s assigned and family study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth floor of Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library is a designated quiet-study floor, and the library lists quiet study there among its floor services.
cards.source_title: Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available first come, first served when the library is open; quiet-study guidance asks users to silence devices and keep conversations quiet.

cards.title: Main Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Main Library, multiple floors
cards.notes: Reserve a room before meeting your group, then use the table, chairs, and whiteboard to outline tasks, review notes, or plan a presentation.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms with standard collaborative furniture and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: UA students can reserve Main Library group study rooms, which have tables, chairs, and whiteboards, for up to four hours at a time.
cards.source_title: Group study rooms | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: UA students, faculty, and staff may reserve up to four hours at a time and 24 total hours weekly; unreserved rooms are first come, first served.

cards.title: Weaver Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library, multiple floors
cards.notes: Book a Weaver room for a small project session and make the whiteboard your shared agenda; release the space if your group will not arrive.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms distributed across Weaver’s science and engineering library.
cards.evidence_claim: UA students can reserve group study rooms at Albert B. Weaver Science-Engineering Library; standard rooms include tables, chairs, and whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Group study rooms | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve up to four hours at a time and 24 hours weekly; reservations are forfeited after 15 minutes, and unreserved rooms are first come, first served.

cards.title: Maker Studio
cards.subtitle: CATalyst Studios, Main Library B203
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from making or prototyping, then drop in to use the studio; ask staff about equipment before starting unfamiliar work.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in maker environment for hands-on academic projects.
cards.evidence_claim: CATalyst Studios’ Maker Studio is in Main Library B203 and can be used without a reservation for projects involving equipment such as 3D printing, sewing, laser cutting, and more.
cards.source_title: CATalyst Studios spaces | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for the Maker Studio. Entry to the makerspace and surrounding studios has no membership cost; some materials have charges.

cards.title: Virtual Reality (VR) Studio
cards.subtitle: CATalyst Studios, Main Library B202
cards.notes: Use the drop-in VR studio when a course project needs immersive media; check with staff on equipment availability and any setup needed for your session.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in CATalyst space for virtual-reality and multimedia projects.
cards.evidence_claim: CATalyst Studios’ Virtual Reality Studio is in Main Library B202, supports virtual-reality and multimedia projects, and does not require a space reservation.
cards.source_title: CATalyst Studios spaces | University of Arizona Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for the space. CATalyst says it is open to everyone, although some equipment or materials may have separate requirements or costs.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along and beside Historic Fourth Avenue, the campus-adjacent commercial corridor southwest of the University of Arizona.

cards.title: Browse used books
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 214 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Walk the Fourth Avenue corridor to this used-book and ephemera shop; check its listed hours before making a dedicated stop.
cards.short_summary: A named Fourth Avenue shop for used books and ephemera.
cards.evidence_claim: Book Stop is at 214 N. 4th Avenue and specializes in used books and ephemera.
cards.source_title: Book Stop | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Wed–Sat 11am–7pm; Sun noon–5pm; closed Mon–Tue.

cards.title: Find all-ages books
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 411 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Add this independent bookstore to a Fourth Avenue walk when you want books for all ages plus cards and gifts.
cards.short_summary: An independent, solar-powered bookstore on the corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Antigone Books is an independent, 100% solar-powered bookstore carrying books for all ages, gifts, and cards at 411 N. 4th Ave.
cards.source_title: Antigone Books | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Tue–Sat 10am–7pm; Sun 11am–5pm; closed Monday.

cards.title: Shop a consumer co-op
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 412 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Use this Fourth Avenue grocery stop for a cooperative-market visit; the listing states that both members and non-members may enter.
cards.short_summary: A full-service consumer cooperative open to members and non-members.
cards.evidence_claim: Food Conspiracy Co-op, at 412 N. 4th Ave., is Tucson's only full-service consumer cooperative and is open to non-members and members alike.
cards.source_title: Food Conspiracy Co-op | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: daily, 7am–9pm.

cards.title: Look through vinyl
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 636 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Head north on Fourth Avenue for a record-shop stop with new and used vintage vinyl, CDs, turntables, speakers, and amps.
cards.short_summary: A named shop for records and audio gear on Fourth Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Hurricane Records at 636 N. 4th Ave. sells new and used vintage vinyl records, CDs, turntables, speakers, compact amps, and shirts.
cards.source_title: Hurricane Records | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Tue–Wed noon–5pm; Thu–Fri 11am–5pm; Sat 10am–5pm; Sun 11am–4pm; closed Monday.

cards.title: See handmade goods
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 422 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Make a short Fourth Avenue stop for handmade goods with a local and sustainability-focused assortment from a women-run business.
cards.short_summary: A Fourth Avenue shop centered on handmade and local goods.
cards.evidence_claim: Pop-Cycle, at 422 N. 4th Ave., is a women-run business specializing in handmade, local goods with a focus on sustainability.
cards.source_title: Pop-Cycle | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: daily, 11am–5pm.

cards.title: Pick out a floral gift
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 440 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Stop at this Fourth Avenue floral and gift shop to browse hand-poured candles and work associated with local artists.
cards.short_summary: An artisan floral and gift shop on Historic Fourth Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: 440 & Co. is an artisan floral and gift shop at 440 N. 4th Avenue; its listing describes hand-poured candles and partnerships with local artists.
cards.source_title: 440 & Co. | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: daily, 10am–5pm.

cards.title: Source DIY upholstery materials
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 246 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Visit this corridor shop when a project needs foam, fabric, canvas, batting, thread, piping, or upholstery tools.
cards.short_summary: A named Fourth Avenue supplier for upholstery materials.
cards.evidence_claim: A Foam & Fabric Place at 246 N. 4th Ave. specializes in upholstery supplies including foam, fabrics, vinyl, canvas, batting, threads, piping, and tools.
cards.source_title: A Foam & Fabric Place | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Mon–Fri 9am–5:30pm; closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: View Mexican art
cards.subtitle: Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 545 N. 4th Ave.
cards.notes: Include this gallery on a northbound Fourth Avenue walk to see its listed assortment of Mexican art during open hours.
cards.short_summary: A gallery on Fourth Avenue with Mexican art.
cards.evidence_claim: La Iguana Art Gallery is at 545 N. 4th Ave. and has a large assortment of Mexican art.
cards.source_title: La Iguana Art Gallery | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Tue–Sun 11am–5pm; closed Monday.

cards.title: Browse antiques nearby
cards.subtitle: Beside the Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 537 N. 6th Ave.
cards.notes: Step one block west of Fourth Avenue to this named antique shop, then use its listed daily schedule to time your visit.
cards.short_summary: An antiques destination immediately beside the Fourth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Sixth Avenue Antiques is a shop located at 537 N. 6th Avenue in Tucson.
cards.source_title: Sixth Avenue Antiques | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Mon–Sat 10am–6pm; Sun 11am–5pm.

cards.title: Browse art for home spaces
cards.subtitle: Beside the Historic Fourth Avenue corridor — 418 E. 7th St.
cards.notes: Turn east from Fourth Avenue onto 7th Street for this gallery, whose listing describes art intended for every room of a home.
cards.short_summary: A named 7th Street gallery beside the Fourth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Heart of the Sun Gallery is located at 418 E. 7th Street and describes its offering as art for every room.
cards.source_title: Heart of the Sun Gallery | Tucson's Historic Fourth Avenue
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Sun–Mon 11am–5pm; Fri 11am–6pm; Sat noon–6pm; closed Tue–Thu.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Arizona rituals and recurring expressions of Wildcat spirit.

cards.title: Say “Bear Down!”
cards.subtitle: University-wide Wildcat rallying cry
cards.notes: Use the university’s official motto as a greeting or cheer at an appropriate campus or athletics gathering; its origin is tied to John “Button” Salmon.
cards.short_summary: Arizona’s century-old two-word rallying cry.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Arizona identifies “Bear Down” as its official motto and an enduring rallying cry originating with John Byrd “Button” Salmon in 1926.
cards.source_title: Bear Down 100
cards.access_notes: No special access is inherent to using the motto; follow event rules when cheering.

cards.title: Listen for “Bear Down, Arizona”
cards.subtitle: University fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the song at an Arizona sporting event or from the campus bell tower, then join only if you know the words and event etiquette allows.
cards.short_summary: The fight song built from Arizona’s signature phrase.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni reports that Jack K. Lee wrote “Bear Down, Arizona,” and that it is played at University of Arizona sporting events and from the campus bell tower daily.
cards.source_title: The 'Bear Down' Story
cards.access_notes: Sporting-event entry rules apply; bell-tower play is heard from public campus areas.

cards.title: Catch the second fight song
cards.subtitle: Arizona athletics and bell-tower music
cards.notes: Notice the companion song, “Fight, Wildcats, Fight,” during athletics programming or bell-tower play; it is distinct from “Bear Down, Arizona.”
cards.short_summary: Arizona’s other regularly played fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that Douglas Holsclaw’s “Fight, Wildcats, Fight” is played throughout University of Arizona sporting events and from the campus bell tower daily.
cards.source_title: The 'Bear Down' Story
cards.access_notes: Sporting-event entry rules apply; bell-tower play is heard from public campus areas.

cards.title: See the Salmon-bust tribute
cards.subtitle: Near Lowell-Stevens Football Facility
cards.notes: Before a home football game, watch the team’s tribute at John “Button” Salmon’s bust; keep clear of the team procession and facility operations.
cards.short_summary: Football players touch Salmon’s bust before home games.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni documents that, since 2013, Arizona football players pass and touch John “Button” Salmon’s bust while completing the Wildcat Walk before every home game.
cards.source_title: The 'Bear Down' Story
cards.access_notes: View only from areas open to the public on home-game days; respect event and team-route controls.

cards.title: Line up for the Wildcat Walk
cards.subtitle: Cherry Avenue route to Arizona Stadium
cards.notes: Before a home football game, use public viewing areas along the announced route to greet the arriving team, band, cheerleaders, and mascots.
cards.short_summary: A pregame procession from the Mall to Arizona Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Athletics introduced the Wildcat Walk as a game-day tradition in which the football team, Pride of Arizona, cheerleaders, and mascots proceed down Cherry Avenue toward Arizona Stadium.
cards.source_title: Wildcats to Debut New Game Day Tradition
cards.access_notes: Occurs before Arizona home football games; use designated public areas and follow current game-day instructions.

cards.title: Watch “A” Mountain light up
cards.subtitle: Sentinel Peak during Homecoming
cards.notes: During Homecoming programming, view the red-lit “A” from a lawful public vantage point; do not approach the lighting operation or restricted terrain.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming begins with a red flare-lit “A” on Sentinel Peak.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arizona News describes the traditional lighting of “A” Mountain with red flares as the kickoff of Homecoming festivities and Spirit Week.
cards.source_title: Desert Bound: Celebrating Wildcat pride during Spirit Week and Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Homecoming/Spirit Week; view from lawful public spaces and follow fire-safety directions.

cards.title: Join Homecoming week
cards.subtitle: Annual University of Arizona reunion tradition
cards.notes: Check the university’s Homecoming schedule for public programs that fit your interests, then attend the listed campus or community events as directed.
cards.short_summary: A University of Arizona tradition dating to 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that University of Arizona Homecoming dates to 1914 and was suspended only during World War I and World War II.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions
cards.access_notes: Events and access vary by the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Follow the Territorial Cup
cards.subtitle: Arizona–Arizona State football rivalry trophy
cards.notes: Follow the annual Arizona–Arizona State football matchup and learn the trophy’s long history before taking part in any official game-day programming.
cards.short_summary: The trophy tradition reaches back to Arizona’s first football season.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that the Territorial Cup tradition goes back to 1899, the year the University of Arizona first fielded a football team.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions
cards.access_notes: Game attendance and related events are subject to current ticketing and venue rules.

cards.title: Spot both Wildcats
cards.subtitle: University of Arizona’s paired mascots
cards.notes: Look for Wilbur and Wilma at their respective athletics appearances, and enjoy the performance without trying to identify the student performers.
cards.short_summary: Arizona’s mascot tradition features a married Wildcat pair.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni documents that Wilbur and Wilma met in 1986 and were married before the Arizona State football game that year; their performer identities remain secret until the final regular-season home basketball game.
cards.source_title: Wilbur and Wilma
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the athletics schedule and venue rules.

cards.title: Meet up at Bear Down Friday
cards.subtitle: Main Gate Square before home football games
cards.notes: Before a home football game, check current event details for the Main Gate Square gathering, including the Pride of Arizona march-through and spirit programming.
cards.short_summary: A pregame Friday gathering centered on Wildcat cheers.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Athletics identifies Bear Down Friday at Main Gate Square as a ZonaZoo event before home football games, featuring the Pride of Arizona, Arizona Athletics speakers, Pomline, Wilbur, and Wilma.
cards.source_title: ZonaZoo
cards.access_notes: Arizona Athletics says this occurs the day before home football games; confirm current event details before going.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Arizona, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, a study stop, and optional scheduled activities for a first Tucson weekend.

cards.title: Start at Old Main
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · historic campus core
cards.notes: Begin with a slow lap around the wraparound porch and grounds, then use the building’s interpretive history to orient yourself to the original campus.
cards.short_summary: See the university’s oldest building and a central historic landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Main is the University of Arizona’s oldest building; it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972.
cards.source_title: Historic Preservation at the University of Arizona
cards.access_notes: The university’s Spirit & Traditions page describes Old Main as having a wraparound porch with rocking chairs.

cards.title: Pause at Berger Memorial Fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · immediately west of Old Main
cards.notes: Stop at the octagonal fountain before continuing across campus; read its memorial purpose and keep the visit respectful of the people it commemorates.
cards.short_summary: A named historic fountain beside Old Main with a documented memorial purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: Berger Memorial Fountain, immediately west of Old Main, memorializes UA students who died in World War I and was dedicated in 1920.
cards.source_title: Historic Preservation at the University of Arizona
cards.access_notes: Located immediately west of Old Main, according to the university preservation page.

cards.title: Walk through Krutch Garden
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · east of Old Main on the Campus Mall
cards.notes: Follow the paths and pause at the distinctive boojum and Sonoran native plants; use the garden page as a lightweight plant-identification guide.
cards.short_summary: A historic Campus Mall garden featuring Sonoran native plants.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joseph Wood Krutch Garden stands east of Old Main and includes Sonoran native plants, including cactus species and a boojum tree.
cards.source_title: The Joseph Wood Krutch Garden
cards.access_notes: The garden page describes shaded seating and a self-guided tour option; stay on established paths around plantings.

cards.title: Choose a self-guided arboretum tour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus-wide walking activity
cards.notes: Pick the Arboretum History, Edible Landscapes, Sonoran Native Plants, or Medicinal Plants booklet and make a short route that fits your energy.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, campus-wide way to notice named trees and gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Campus Arboretum offers self-guided tour booklets that direct visitors to campus locations with described trees.
cards.source_title: Guided and Self-Directed Tours
cards.access_notes: Tour options and available booklets are listed by the UA Campus Arboretum; confirm any current tour logistics before setting out.

cards.title: Regroup at the Student Union Memorial Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 1303 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical reset point: locate student services, check event postings, and meet up before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building that houses student-focused services and event spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union Memorial Center is at the heart of campus and hosts services including Meal Plans, CatCard, and the Basic Needs Center.
cards.source_title: Student Unions Overview
cards.access_notes: Address: 1303 E. University Blvd. Check individual services or events for current availability.

cards.title: Find the U.S.S. Arizona Bell
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Student Union Memorial Center tower
cards.notes: While at the Union, look up toward the bell tower and read the memorial context; the bell is preserved in the tower as a dedicated memorial.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic bell preserved in the Student Union tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union preserves one of two original bells salvaged from the U.S.S. Arizona; it is dedicated to those who died on the battleship.
cards.source_title: Student Unions Overview
cards.access_notes: The bell is preserved in the Student Unions tower; view it as part of the building rather than treating it as a separate public program.

cards.title: Make a Main Library plan
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 1510 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Take a floor-by-floor look, choose a quiet or group-study area for a future session, and note the Tech Toolshed and CATalyst Studios.
cards.short_summary: A flexible study and creation stop with quiet floors and technology services.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library provides study, collaboration, technology, and research spaces, including quiet study rooms and CATalyst Studios.
cards.source_title: Main Library
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary by date; check the library’s current hours page before going.

cards.title: Add Flandrau to the afternoon
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 1601 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Check the day’s program before heading over, then allow time to explore the science-center and planetarium visit at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A campus science center and planetarium with published visitor hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Flandrau Science Center & Planetarium is located at 1601 E. University Blvd. and lists Tuesday–Sunday visitor hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Hours and Parking | Flandrau Science Center & Planetarium
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the page says admission must be purchased, so confirm current programming and tickets.

cards.title: Try a beginner bouldering workshop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · SouthREC
cards.notes: Check the current workshop schedule, wear closed-toe shoes, and start with the staff-led introduction rather than attempting advanced moves on your own.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Campus Recreation climbing activity with beginner-friendly instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: Outdoor Recreation offers weekly bouldering workshops, and its FAQ says no prior climbing experience is needed for climbing workshops.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation FAQs and Policies
cards.access_notes: Workshops are regularly scheduled but can be canceled; closed-toe shoes are required in the bouldering area. Check the current schedule and access requirements.

cards.title: Learn the Bear Down story
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · campus spirit tradition
cards.notes: Before a game or campus event, read the university’s account of the motto and listen for it in context rather than assuming a particular event is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A documented University of Arizona rallying cry with a specific campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: “Bear Down!” became the University of Arizona rallying cry after student body president and quarterback John Byrd “Button” Salmon’s 1926 final message to his coach.
cards.source_title: Spirit & Traditions
cards.access_notes: This is a campus tradition rather than a guaranteed scheduled event; consult official Athletics or campus calendars for current events.
